p: Torah learning became implanted in their hearts, etc.;
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts, etc."
אִם כֵּן, מָה הָיָה צָרִיךְ לָהֶם
if so, what need did they have
since the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts?
As Moshe Rabbeinu answered the angels:
"Is there a yetzer hara among you?"
it says in the Mechilta (Yisro, BaChodesh 2),
if a person heard one mitzvah,
they cause him to hear many mitzvos.
And similarly it is expounded in the Gemara
on the part of Hashem Yisbarach:
that He gave them one positive mitzvah,
the root of all the positive mitzvos,
Torah learning became implanted in their hearts.
And He gave them one prohibition,
the root of all the prohibitions,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נֶעֱקַר מִלִּבָּם הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
and through this the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts —
but only for the time being.
and revealed to Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom,
that it would return to its place,
nevertheless they would have the strength
And He gave them "six hundred thirteen kinds of counsel,"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב פב, ב);
(as it says in the holy Zohar II 82b);
so that the utterance "I am" be fixed in the heart
and the yetzer hara be uprooted from the foolish heart.
when the festival of Shavuos arrives,
then is the time to bring about
that the yetzer hara be uprooted from the foolish heart.
For this reason it says in the holy Zohar
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג צז, ב, בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא):
where 'a sin-offering to Hashem' is written."
the korbanos were offered every year,
and on the contrary, in the first year
they did not yet offer the korbanos.
the yetzer hara already returned to its place
דַּבֵּר אַתָּה עִמָּנוּ וְנִשְׁמָעָה וְגוֹ׳ (שְׁמוֹת כ, טז)?
"You speak with us and we will hear, etc." (Shemos 20:16)?
when this day of Atzeres comes,
that is the time to bring about
that the yetzer hara be uprooted from the heart of Yisrael,
as in the first year of Matan Torah;
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי לָא כְּתִיב חַטָּאת לַה׳.
and therefore "a sin-offering to Hashem" is not written.
For every year Yisrael are called
in the aspect of a bride under her chuppah,
and it is the time to receive
when Torah learning was implanted in their hearts
and the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts.
there would have been "engraved on the Luchos" —
freedom from the Angel of Death
וְהוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע
and the Angel of Death is the yetzer hara
And so the time of Matan Torah
is for the yetzer hara to be uprooted
and Torah learning to be implanted
in the heart of each one according to his level.
"And you shall be a treasure to Me from among all the peoples,
כִּי לִי כׇּל הָאָרֶץ (שְׁמוֹת יט, ה).
for all the earth is Mine" (Shemos 19:5).
וְלֹא תֹּאמְרוּ אַתֶּם לְבַדְּכֶם שֶׁלִּי וְכוּלֵּי;
"And do not say that you alone are Mine, etc.;
for all the earth is Mine,
and they are as nothing in My eyes and before Me."
This is difficult: what is the novelty?
After all, the nations refused to accept the Torah
that they will be a treasure from among all the peoples
But it is said in the name of
the Yehudi HaKadosh, zecher tzaddik livrachah,
That is: after they accept the Torah,
then "you shall be to Me" like a segulah;
even if, chas v'shalom, they become corrupted
and are exiled among the nations,
הֲלֹא אָח עֵשָׂו לְיַעֲקֹב (מַלְאָכִי א, ב);
"Is not Esav a brother to Yaakov?" (Malachi 1:2);
that is, even if Yaakov should act,
chas v'shalom, like the deeds of Esav,
or if Esav should resemble in his deeds
And this will be so even in exile;
and this is the meaning of "from among all the peoples" —
even when you are in the midst of the peoples.
And the reason for the exiles
is "for all the earth is Mine,"
in the manner of what it says:
וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כּוּלָּם (נְחֶמְיָה ט, ו);
"And You give life to them all" (Nechemyah 9:6);
and in every nation there is some vitality
they will bring out the holy sparks
This is along the lines of what we said
"so that converts be added to them" —
that what is meant is also
This is difficult: it should have written together,
"And you shall be to Me a treasure and a kingdom of Kohanim."
But according to what was said, it is understood:
what it said, "And you shall be a treasure to Me,"
when they will be in the midst of exile,
the generation of the wilderness whom He was addressing —
"shall be to Me a kingdom of Kohanim,"
free all their days only for Torah,
and He fed them the man
and gave them to drink the water of the well,
and the Torah settled in their hearts
(as Chazal say, Tanchuma, the beginning of Parshas Beshalach);
וְלֹא נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא לְאוֹכְלֵי מָן
and the Torah was given only to those who ate the man
and second to them are those who eat terumah;
therefore they are a kingdom of Kohanim.
"For the entire congregation, all of them are holy,
and Hashem is in their midst" (Bamidbar 16:3).
And since this was written in the Torah,
for the Torah would not have written it,
even though he truly said it
the utterance of "I am" and "You shall have no other,"
even though the yetzer hara returned
